title: Finite constant component quotient of an affine algebraic group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist a finite abstract group $P$ and a surjective $k$-group-scheme homomorphism $c:G\to P_k$, where $P_k=\coprod_{a\in P}\operatorname{Spec}k=\operatorname{Spec}(k^P)$ is the affine finite-type constant group scheme, with multiplication, inverse and identity induced by those of $P$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The nonempty subsets $|c|^{-1}(\{a\})$, for $a\in P$, are exactly the connected components of $|G|$. Here a connected component is a maximal connected subset, and connectedness is as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]. In particular the fibre over $1\in P$ is the component containing the identity of $G$. No smoothness, reducedness, commutativity or characteristic-zero assumption on $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 2(g), Proposition 2.37(b),(d), printed pp.51-52, with the construction preceding it and Remark 2.39(a). Over an algebraically closed field the finite etale component group is constant.

proof.text: Write $C$ for the identity component and $P$ for the set of connected components of $G$. By lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates, $P$ is finite, every component $D$ is clopen, and there is $g_D\in G(k)$ whose left translation identifies the open subscheme $C$ with the open subscheme $G_D=D$. In particular $g_D=t_{g_D}(e)$ lies in $D$, so every component has a rational point. By lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component, $C$ is geometrically irreducible: the finite-type hypothesis implies locally finite type, as required there. Each $G_D$ is geometrically irreducible too, since the translation isomorphism base changes to an isomorphism over every field extension. These statements apply to the original open subschemes, including their nilpotents.

source.place: Proposition 1.34 and Section 2(g), construction before Proposition 2.37, printed pp.16 and 51; geometric irreducibility also Stacks Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component).

proof.text: For $D,E\in P$, lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field makes $G_D\times_kG_E$ irreducible, hence connected. Its image under multiplication is a nonempty connected subset of $G$, so lies in a unique component; define that component to be $DE$. It contains $g_Dg_E$. Thus, for arbitrary rational points $x\in D(k)$ and $y\in E(k)$, the component of $xy$ is $DE$, independently of the chosen representatives. Inversion similarly sends $G_D$ into a unique component, denoted $D^{-1}$, containing $g_D^{-1}$. The map $q:G(k)\to P$ taking a rational point to its component is surjective by step 1 and satisfies $q(xy)=q(x)q(y)$ and $q(x^{-1})=q(x)^{-1}$. The group laws on $G(k)$ therefore give the laws on $P$: choose representatives $x,y,z$ to obtain $(DE)F=q((xy)z)=q(x(yz))=D(EF)$; $q(e)D=q(ex)=D=q(xe)=Dq(e)$; and $DD^{-1}=q(xx^{-1})=q(e)=q(x^{-1}x)=D^{-1}D$. Consequently $P$ is a finite abstract group whose identity is $C$.

source.place: Section 2(g), construction of the group on components before Proposition 2.37, printed p.51; connected products: Stacks Tag 038F (lemma-bijection-irreducible-components).

proof.text: Form $Q=\coprod_{D\in P}\operatorname{Spec}k$ with inclusions $j_D$, using lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family. Its summands are disjoint clopen singletons. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies $Q_D\times_kQ_E$ with the open subset cut out by these two summands in $Q\times_kQ$; these subsets cover because both projections land in some summand. Each is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}k$, by the fibre-product universal property over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. On it define multiplication to be the structural map followed by $j_{DE}$. Define inversion on $Q_D$ by $j_{D^{-1}}$, and the identity by $j_C$. Glue along these disjoint open covers. Each group identity holds on each summand of its source: the two maps have the same label by the group law of $P$, and the unique $k$-map to that copy of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Gluing uniqueness gives the scheme identities, including associativity on the triple open cover. This makes $Q$ the constant group scheme $P_k$. The finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum lemma identifies $Q$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(k^P)$, with $j_D$ induced by evaluation at $D$. This is affine and of finite type: the finitely many coordinate idempotents generate $k^P$ over $k$, since $(a_D)_D=\sum_Da_D\delta_D$.

source.place: Section 2(g), constant component-group construction, printed p.51; Stacks Tags 01JB/01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes), 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), and 00ED (algebra-lemma-spec-product).

proof.text: On the clopen cover $G=\bigcup_{D\in P}G_D$, define $c|_{G_D}$ to be $G_D\to\operatorname{Spec}k\xrightarrow{j_D}Q$. The overlaps are empty, so the scheme-morphism gluing lemma gives a $k$-morphism $c:G\to Q$. We check $c\circ m_G=m_Q\circ(c\times c)$ as morphisms, rather than just on rational points. The opens $G_D\times_kG_E$ cover $G\times_kG$ by the open-fibre-product lemma. By step 2 multiplication sends each of these opens into $G_{DE}$, so its restriction factors uniquely through that open subscheme by lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme. On this source, both displayed composites are the structural $k$-map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ followed by $j_{DE}$. Hence they are equal there, and gluing uniqueness proves equality globally. Similarly on $G_D$ both inverse composites equal its structural map followed by $j_{D^{-1}}$, while $c\circ e_G=j_C=e_Q$. These are precisely the homomorphism identities for group schemes.

source.place: Section 2(g), homomorphism preceding Proposition 2.37, printed p.51; Stacks Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens), and 01JB/01JC (gluing mapping property).

proof.text: By its definition on the disjoint open pieces, $|c|^{-1}(\{D\})=D$ for every $D\in P$: points of $G_D$ map to the $D$-th summand, and no other summand has that point. Each $D$ is nonempty, so $|c|$ is surjective. Thus these fibres are exactly the connected components, and the fibre over the group identity $C\in P$ is the component containing $e_G$. All constructions used the original component open subschemes; no reduction or smoothness assumption has entered.

source.place: Proposition 2.37(b),(d), printed pp.51-52, now immediate from the componentwise construction.
